trust_decision.summary: ffgcls2 trusts the file-supplied variable-length string descriptor length (repeat -> twidth) as fitting the fixed stack buffer cbuff; the size check (ntodo*twidth <= sizeof(cbuff)) is evaluated only after ffgbyt/ffgbytoff have already filled cbuff.

landing_point.why: Advisory names ffgcls2 in getcols.c; the only bounds check in the function sits at getcols.c:927, directly below the reads.

fix_sites.entry_point: fits_read_col_str (ffgcvs) / fits_read_colnull (ffgcfs) / fits_read_col(TSTRING) (ffgcv) on a variable-length 'PA'/'QA' column
same public APIs; strided-read branch (incre != twidth)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No O2 site or O8 route found; the fixed-width TSTRING path is already guarded by ffgcprll's COL_TOO_WIDE check (fitscore.c:5783-5789), so a solver would correctly leave it alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Fixed-width string columns wider than IOBUFLEN (2880) but below DBUFFSIZE (28800) are legitimately read one string at a time; a fix that caps twidth at IOBUFLEN or rejects maxelem==1 reads would break them. Var-length strings up to DBUFFSIZE-1 bytes must still read.

O6_input_shapes: variable-length string column whose heap descriptor length exceeds sizeof(cbuff), contiguous read (getcols.c:920)

O7_producer.where: fitscore.c:5746-5750 (ffgcprll sets twidth=nelem=1 for -TSTRING, so its COL_TOO_WIDE guard never sees the real descriptor length)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second var-length string reader inside ffgcls (e.g. a TSTRING-with-TDISP branch) that reads the descriptor length into a local buffer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ffgcls already formats every other column type into local tmpstr/cbuff-style buffers; a maintainer adding var-string display handling could copy ffgcls2's read sequence.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a writemode 15-18 (TSTRING-as-TBYTE) var-length reader that sets repeat=twidth but fails to bound ntodo by maxelem
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This special case already rewrites repeat from twidth for var columns; a copied reader that skipped the minvalue(remain,maxelem) clamp would be a natural sibling.

O9_family: memory safety: stack buffer overflow (out-of-bounds write) from untrusted length field in file metadata

O10_build.toolchain: CMake or autoconf/make, C compiler; zlib (optional libcurl, bzip2)
O10_build.project_tests: No unit tests for this area; only testprog.c / cookbook.c smoke programs, plus utilities/fitsverify which reads var-length strings (utilities/fvrf_data.c:438-450).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move the existing ntodo*twidth > sizeof(cbuff) check above the ffgbyt/ffgbytoff calls (which is very likely the published fix itself).

out_of_scope_notes: ffgcls2 also writes twidth+1 bytes into the caller's array[ii] (getcols.c:939-958) with twidth taken from the file descriptor; callers must size buffers themselves (fitsverify does so at utilities/fvrf_data.c:349,439). This is a caller-contract issue, not pursued.
Expression parser rejects variable-length columns (eval_f.c:2521-2527), and the other var-length readers bound ntodo by maxelem, so they do not reach this sink.
unverified: The provided fix diff (div-84085.fix.diff) contains only the merge-commit header and no hunks; fix sites getcols.c:920/922 are inferred from the PR branch name 'fix/ffgcls2-buffer-bounds', the candidate metadata (2 sites, 1 file, restructured, single compact hunk) and the ordering of the check after the reads at the pinned commit.
Whether the published fix also changes the zero-length var-string behaviour (ntodo*twidth < 1 -> READ_ERROR at getcols.c:927) is unknown.
